title: Walking Tour of a Loʻi Kalo

content.html:
Kalo

The kalo plant is the foundation of Hawaiian agriculture and central to Hawaiian cosmology — in the Kumulipo, kalo is the elder sibling of humanity.

Kalo is pronounced KAH-loh.

ʻAuwai

The ʻauwai is the irrigation channel that diverts cool stream water through the loʻi. Traditional Hawaiian water rights guaranteed downstream loʻi enough flow to keep kalo healthy.

Huli

The huli is the top of a harvested kalo corm, replanted to start the next generation. Each loʻi cycles through harvest and replanting on a roughly 9-12 month rhythm.
